title: Positivity of the spectral one-norm
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function that is not identically zero. Then its spectral one-norm is strictly positive: $\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|\widehat f(S)|>0$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. If a real cube function $f$ is not identically zero, then its spectral one-norm $\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|\widehat f(S)|$ is strictly positive.
